newsitem.title: USA: Patriot American sees FFO above $3.01/shr.
newsitem.headline: Patriot American sees FFO above $3.01/shr.

text.p: Patriot American Hospitality Inc said Tuesday it expects 1996 funds from operations to be above the consensus analysts' estimate of $3.01 a share.
"We'll do better than $3.01," chief financial officer Rex Stewart said in an interview following a presentation to investors here. The company became public 11 months ago.

The real estate investment trust also said it expects to increase its dividend toward the end of the year or early next year, based on regulatory requirements that govern what those trusts must pay to shareholders. "As we look toward 1997, we have to increase the dividend rate," Stewart said.
Patriot American, which buys, improves and then leases out hotels, has purchased 18 hotels with 4,744 rooms since its initial public offering and expects to keep that pace in 1997.
"Our goal for next year would be to stay on the same pace," president and chief operating officer Thomas Lattin said in the interview.
The company looks to acquire four-star hotels in major markets or tourist destinations that have high barriers to new hotels entering the market, Lattin told investors.
The company has several hotels in Texas, with others in Seattle, Atlanta, Boston, southern California and other markets.
Among the markets the company is looking to enter are Chicago, where an acqusition is expected this week, Washington, D.C., Phoenix and San Francisco, Lattin said.
Patriot American sets a base level of rent for each hotel, then receives 70 percent of increases in room revenues, higher than many competitors, he said.
In terms of funding acquisitions, Patriot American has a line of credit of $250 million, which helps it quickly close deals, Stewart said.
The company also sold 5.5 million shares in a public offering in July, with an additional 646,700 shares to underwriters to cover over-allotments.
Patriot American expects examine other forms of debt to pay down its line of credit later this year or early next year, Stewart said.
